method: PatAgent uses the complete synced blog for retrieval and this curated catalog for stable audit-gate citations.

sources.title: Practical Cheminformatics Index
principles: Use the unified index to discover archived Blogger and current GitHub Pages posts.
Treat the blog as an evolving corpus and refresh it instead of freezing a one-time summary.

sources.title: We Need Better Benchmarks for Machine Learning in Drug Discovery
principles: Validate structures, representation consistency, stereochemistry, duplicates, labels, and assay artifacts.
Prefer relevant, clearly defined endpoints measured consistently under realistic ranges and cutoffs.
Preserve provenance, experimental error, reference standards, and predefined train/validation/test splits.
Use benchmarks to expose where methods fail, and maintain benchmark versions over time.

sources.title: Getting Real with Molecular Property Prediction
principles: Explore distributions before modeling and compare against a simple constant or empirical baseline.
Estimate the ceiling imposed by experimental error and report bootstrapped confidence intervals.
Assess whether training and test chemical spaces differ, including adversarial validation.
Use multiple realistic split strategies and prefer an understandable simple method when performance is practically equivalent.

sources.title: Multiple Comparisons, Non-Parametric Statistics, and Post-Hoc Tests
principles: Inspect distributions and dependence before choosing a statistical test.
Do not apply an independent-sample t-test to repeated measurements of the same molecular cases.
Correct for multiple comparisons; Holm adjustment is often preferable to an increasingly conservative Bonferroni correction.
Plot complete distributions rather than relying on means and error bars alone.

sources.title: How Good Could (Should) My Models Be?
principles: Simulate measurement error to estimate an attainable correlation distribution.
Investigate results that exceed a plausible ceiling given experimental uncertainty.

sources.title: Some Thoughts on Splitting Chemical Datasets
principles: Random splits can be optimistic when test molecules resemble training examples.
Scaffold splits can also be optimistic because different scaffolds may remain highly similar.
Compare split difficulty and train-test similarity; Butina or temporal-style splits can be more informative, with caveats.
Treat splitting as an experimental-design decision, not a default library argument.

sources.title: Why Don't Machine Learning Models Extrapolate?
principles: Compare prediction ranges with the response and chemical ranges represented in training data.
Set realistic expectations for unsupported regions and include simple linear or empirical controls.

sources.title: The Trouble With Tautomers
principles: Algorithmic canonical tautomers need not represent experimentally populated species.
Use canonical tautomeric identifiers to detect duplicates, but do not automatically replace model inputs without evidence.
Measure the actual sensitivity of predictions to tautomer representation relative to experimental and resampling variability.

sources.title: Just Because You Published It Doesn't Mean It's Right
principles: Evaluate models on realistic dynamic ranges and test sets that are not near-neighbor copies of training data.
Compare against a null predictor and separate impressive-looking correlation from practical utility.
Published benchmark status is not a substitute for dataset quality review and statistical method comparison.

sources.title: We Still Haven't Found What We're Looking For - The Continuing Evolution of Protein-Ligand Co-Folding Methods
principles: Stratify pose performance by protein, pocket, and ligand similarity to training data.
Separate top-ranked performance from an oracle best-of-N pose result.
Include allosteric systems and verify pocket placement because orthosteric evidence can dominate predictions.
Avoid strong affinity or generalization claims without prospective experimental evidence.

sources.title: Generative Molecular Design - We Need to Raise the Bar
principles: Report chemical validity, uniqueness, and the most similar training examples for proposed hits.
Distinguish model contribution from human selection and post-processing.
Assess synthesis, nuisance chemistry, multi-objective tradeoffs, and experimental validation.
Release enough code, data, and procedure for others to reproduce and extend the work.

sources.title: Comparing Classification Models - A Practical Tutorial
principles: Do not conclude that one model wins from cross-validation means alone.
Use statistically rigorous comparison of paired model results and report their distributions.

sources.title: Evaluation Guidelines for Machine Learning Tools in the Chemical Sciences
principles: Define the task and intended use before choosing data, splits, metrics, and baselines.
Separate training, validation, and test roles and assess domain, uncertainty, robustness, and reproducibility.
Match evaluation design to the chemical-science question instead of relying on generic ML scores.

sources.title: Modeling, Informatics, and the Quest for Reproducibility
principles: Make software, structures, data, and supporting information accessible enough to reproduce computational work.
Record procedures and inputs with the rigor expected of experimental methods.

sources.title: Code Sharing in the Open Science Era
principles: Computational papers should release code or an adequate reproducible implementation.
Capture versions, inputs, and executable details rather than presenting only final tables and plots.

sources.title: Practically Significant Method Comparison Protocols for Machine Learning in Small Molecule Drug Discovery
principles: Use domain-appropriate metrics and statistically rigorous paired comparison protocols.
Report practical effect size and uncertainty, not only statistical significance.
Predefine methods and avoid treating dependent resampling folds as independent observations.

sources.title: Blind Challenges Let Us See the Path Forward for Predictive Models
principles: Use prospective blind challenges to measure progress under realistic conditions.
Pair open high-quality data generation with community evaluation and experimental follow-up.
